scope.platform: Linux/WSL x86_64 host; not a Cortex-M7 or disting NT device benchmark
scope.input: Existing benchmark_vocoder.cpp deterministic sinusoidal carrier/modulator signals
scope.width: 50 static; moving Width15..85 and Formant approximately +/-12 semitones
scope.compiler: Host c++ -O3 -std=c++17; existing host CMSIS objects
scope.timing: Final comparisons use std::clock process CPU time, two runs per case and their median; shared-host wall-time contention excluded
scope.snapshot: Frozen SVF implementation before final 9V output-guard and tiny-state-flush tuning; these timings are not an exact final-binary/device CPU claim

initial_host_wall_time_context.interpretation: Host work increased roughly twofold or more. Exact ratios depend on input/control case and host load; do not extrapolate these wall-time ratios to NT CPU percentages.

synthesis_fusion.numerical_check: Temporary fused prototype produced bitwise-identical outputs and all four filter states versus unfused filtering plus gain across 14 host cascade cases, including 20..18000Hz and Q0.5..120.
synthesis_fusion.decision: Keep unfused production path. CPU-time savings did not meet the requested 10% threshold.

host_ftz_daz_at_depth200.interpretation: Modest measured improvement on this input. Earlier larger wall-time differences were confounded and are intentionally excluded. Production tiny-state flushing avoids relying on platform FTZ configuration.

depth_cache_assessment: The filterbank dominates. With FTZ, static Depth0/70/100/200 medians are approximately435/449/437/446ms. Caching the once-per-block Depth-shape calculation is unlikely to be material; no lookup/power approximation is justified by these results.
production: No performance prototype or approximation was copied into repository DSP by this investigation.
